text:
maria: Quick update — we just enabled the HotStart Warmup policy for short-prefix workloads in prod across us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1. Early aggregate: p50 latency -18%, p99 -9%, per-token GPU cost ~7% lower on sampled traffic.

ben_s: awesome, congrats! do you have the canary dash or the metric queries?

maria: summary metrics are here: https://dashboard.redwood-internal/boards/hotstart-warmup (can view if you have infra-team access). Canary id: hw-canary-2026-03-23. key checks:
```
// PromQL-ish pseudo
avg_over_time(inference_latency_p50{policy="hotstart"}[1h]) - baseline_p50
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
Rolled to 50% traffic in each region for 2 hours before full flip.

suyash: any memory / GPU utilization surprises during the roll? warmup sounds like it might spike mem.

maria: good question — we saw a transient +6% GPU memory footprint during warmup bursts on the smallest models; below the 85% safety threshold. No OOMs. We tuned the prefetch window to 300ms and limited concurrent warmup jobs to 8 per node.

ajenkins: rollback / fail-open strategy?

maria: automatic failover to cold path if any of these triggers fire for >5min in a region:
- p99 increases by >12% vs baseline
- GPU mem >90% sustained 1m
- error rate bump >0.5%
We also keep a one-click rollout revert in the console (devops only).

irene: Dedicated customers (reserved capacity) — were they changed?

maria: Dedicated pools are opted-out by default. We provided an opt-in flag in the Dedicated config -> warmup_policy: OPT_IN | OPT_OUT. Enterprise customers can request a rollout via support.

deploy-bot: canary/hw-canary-2026-03-23 finished: 50->100% flip complete @ 3495000068 :white_check_mark:

ben_s: nice. can we add a short perf note to the runtime release notes and call out recommended config values for slack/llm-short workloads?

maria: yep — adding to release notes now and will paste snippet here once done. TL;DR recommended: prefetch_window=300ms, max_warmup_concurrency=8, short_prefix_threshold=64 tokens.

maria: thanks everyone — this should noticeably improve latency for chatty microservice use-cases. monitoring will keep an eye on tail behaviour over next 72h. :party:
